Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the fix type, the affected provider (gemini Vertex), and the new default model (gemini-3.8-flash). The diff changes the Vertex opus default, the vendor default and catalog, and the related tests, so the title matches the main change. It is somewhat long at 87 characters, but it is specific and accurate.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description fills in the Summary (what and why), Impact (user-facing and developer impact), and most of the Testing section with exact commands and results. The Notes section covers the provider/model path tested, screenshots, and follow-up work. The template's required sections are all present. The main gaps are the unfilled 'Fixes `#N`' placeholder, which has no real issue number, and CI and CodeRabbit status left as pending.
Full details: Risk Surface Disclosed

**Explanation** The check is not triggered by this PR. The reviewed range (4 modified files) changes only Gemini Vertex model identifiers: - `src/integrations/vendors/gemini-vertex.ts`: `defaultModel` changes from `gemini-2.5-flash` to `gemini-3.8-flash`. The two Gemini 2.5 catalog entries become one `gemini-3.8-flash` entry. - `src/utils/model/model.ts` (`getDefaultOpusModel`): the fallback changes from `'gemini-2.5-pro'` to `DEFAULT_GEMINI_VERTEX_MODEL`. The `GEMINI_VERTEX_MODEL` override and the branch condition `getAPIProvider() === 'gemini-vertex'` are unchanged. - Two test files: expectation updates and one new regression test. None of the listed risk surfaces are touched. There are no changes to auth or ADC setup, provider routing or endpoint selection, permissions, outbound network behavior, background execution, startup or config-home logic, skills/plugins/MCP, CI workflows, or release scripts. The vendor's `defaultBaseUrl`, `authMode`, and the `getAPIProvider` branch logic are not changed in the diff. The PR description also states the user-facing impact: Vertex callers of the opus default now receive a Flash model instead of a Pro model. The Gemini API provider is unchanged. The review findings are zero actionable items. Caveat: the default model per provider is a form of provider configuration. A reviewer could argue it sits near provider routing. Even under that reading, the diff does not change which backend receives requests, and no blocker is evident. The model swap is a behavioral change to note in release communication, but it is not a risk-surface change that this check requires the review to call out.
Full details: No Hidden Policy Change

**Explanation** The "No hidden policy change" check passes. The PR changes four files, and the diff matches the stated purpose. Diff evidence: - `src/integrations/vendors/gemini-vertex.ts`: `defaultModel` changes from `gemini-2.5-flash` to `gemini-3.8-flash`. The two Gemini 2.5 catalog entries are replaced by one `gemini-3.8-flash` entry with the same context and output limits. - `src/utils/model/model.ts`: the `gemini-vertex` branch of `getDefaultOpusModel()` changes its fallback from `gemini-2.5-pro` to `DEFAULT_GEMINI_VERTEX_MODEL`. `GEMINI_VERTEX_MODEL` still takes precedence. - Two test files are updated to match. The change is not hidden. The title, the PR description, and the objectives all state the default-model change, the Pro-to-Flash substitution, and the reason (Vertex retirement of the 2.5 models on October 20, 2026). The Gemini API provider and the other providers are not touched. No telemetry, network, permission, or trust-model code changes. The diff contains no unrelated cleanup. Non-blocking note: the change does alter a routing default. With Vertex and no override, `/insights` and the teammate fallback now use a Flash model where they used a Pro model. The PR discloses this. Maintainers may still want to confirm the Flash substitution for the opus-default callers.
